artwork.title: Victorious Youth (Athlete of Fano)
artwork.artist: Unknown Greek sculptor, circle of Lysippos

signals.name: marine-encrustation-residue
signals.interpretation: Residual marine encrustation consistent with prolonged submersion, supporting the reported recovery from the Adriatic.

identifyingRegisters.name: INTERPOL Stolen Works of Art
identifyingRegisters.requires: a theft reported to and recorded by a member-country police force

identifyingRegisters.name: INTERPOL ID-Art
identifyingRegisters.requires: the same police report as the Stolen Works of Art database

identifyingRegisters.name: FBI National Stolen Art File
identifyingRegisters.requires: a law-enforcement submission and a value threshold

identifyingRegisters.name: Carabinieri TPC
identifyingRegisters.requires: an Italian nexus — the archive is national

identifyingRegisters.name: Getty Provenance Index
identifyingRegisters.requires: passage through the European or American art market

identifyingRegisters.name: Art Loss Register
identifyingRegisters.requires: a registered loss, usually by an owner or insurer

weakRegisters.name: Wikidata
weakRegisters.why: Coverage follows scholarly and press attention rather than rule, so its silence carries little information.

blindRegisters.name: Lost Art Database
blindRegisters.why: Holds nazi-era losses; requires a loss connected to Nazi persecution, 1933–45.

blindRegisters.name: ICOM Red Lists
blindRegisters.why: Holds archaeological, colonial losses; requires membership of an at-risk object category from a listed region.

coverage.note: 6 of 9 registers could systematically name this object. Silence here is comparatively informative: records would be expected to exist.
coverage.comparability: This score is comparable only to other well covered objects. Comparison against a structurally uncovered object will understate how little was checked there.

flags.evidence: Timeline cites a repatriation/illicit-excavation event: "Italian court in Pesaro convicted several parties in absentia (including an art dealer and, controversially, a Getty curator) for receiving stolen goods. The Pesaro court's jurisdiction was disputed. The conviction did not result in extradition or return of the statue."
Object history intersects a documented looting/repatriation case.
Pre-acquisition history is incomplete (1 undated event(s); no documented chain before earliest record).

Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "INTERPOL cultural heritage crime unit has referenced the Getty Bronze in the context of Italian repatriation demands for illicitly exported antiquities". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.

Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "Carabinieri TPC has an active repatriation file for the 'Atleta Vittorioso di Fano' (Bronzo di Lisippo), held by the J. Paul Getty Museum". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.

Register source describes this object in theft/looting/restitution terms: "J. Paul Getty Museum acquisition 1977: Victorious Youth (Athlete of Fano). Acquired through German dealer; pre-acquisition provenance disputed with Italy.". Verify against the register itself before relying on it.
2 of 9 registers have no public API and were not searched (INTERPOL SWOA, FBI NSAF, Carabinieri TPC among them). Their silence here means nothing — the official searches must be run by hand.

loanEligibility: Not loaned outside the holding institution while forfeiture proceedings remain open.
